items.title: [Bug]: Hybrid Mamba + MTP silently corrupts requests when the drafter's attention backend lowers the batch-reorder threshold (decode rows run through Mamba prefill kernels)
items.body:
## Summary

With MTP speculative decoding on a hybrid Mamba2 model (`nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Lightning-30B-A3B-BF16`), a request whose first decode step is scheduled while a long prompt is being chunk-prefilled comes back as word salad or an empty loop of special tokens for the rest of its life, from roughly its fifth token on. About 0.2–1% of requests on a mixed workload; up to 7% with a targeted trigger.

Root cause (verified with an in-process probe, see "Probe evidence"): `GPUModelRunner.calculate_reorder_batch_threshold` takes the **minimum** `reorder_batch_threshold` over all attention groups. The MTP drafter's attention backend is auto-selected independently of the target's (`llm_base_proposer.py`: "Never inherit the attention backend from base") and lands on FlashInfer, whose builder reports `1` (`supports_spec_as_decode` is false without the trtllm-gen decode kernel). The target's Mamba2 builders report `1 + k = 4`. With the runner at `1`, `reorder_batch_to_split_decodes_and_prefills` puts a 4-token draft-decode row and a chunked long prefill's *continuing chunk* in the same region and never sorts the decode rows ahead of that chunk. `Mamba2AttentionMetadataBuilder` then calls `split_decodes_and_prefills` at its own threshold `4`, which is positional: every row from the first prefill row on is a prefill. Decode rows behind the continuing chunk are run through `causal_conv1d_fn` / `mamba_chunk_scan_combined_varlen`, which read and write only state slot 0 and never the `k` speculative slots. On a request's first decode step those slots have never been written; the next step's `selective_state_update` reads slot `num_accepted - 1` and the recurrent state is garbage from then on.

The docstring of `calculate_reorder_batch_threshold` says a lower threshold "just may have a performance penalty due to that backend treating decodes as prefills". That holds for token-KV attention; for backends with per-draft recurrent state it is a correctness bug.

## Environment

- vLLM 0.27.1 (both code paths unchanged on `main` at 34b9899), torch 2.13.0+cu130, CUDA 13.0
- 1× NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (sm_120)
- Model: `nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Lightning-30B-A3B-BF16` (NemotronH hybrid Mamba2 + attention + MoE, in-weights MTP head)

Serve command (production):

```
vllm serve nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Lightning-30B-A3B-BF16 --trust-remote-code \
  --max-model-len 262144 --max-num-seqs 96 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 \
  --attention-backend TRITON_ATTN --mamba-backend triton --mamba-cache-mode align \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --async-scheduling \
  --reasoning-parser nemotron_v3 --enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser qwen3_coder \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}'
```

Log excerpt showing the drafter picking a different backend than the target:

```
[cuda.py:422] Using AttentionBackendEnum.TRITON_ATTN backend.
[gpu_model_runner.py:5332] Loading drafter model...
[cuda.py:482] Using FLASHINFER attention backend out of potential backends: ['FLASHINFER', 'TRITON_ATTN'].
```

Prefix caching on (`align`) or off (`none`), `--async-scheduling` on or off, and the KV dtype make no difference. `max_num_batched_tokens` is the default 8192.

## Reproduction

Deterministic-ish trigger: keep ~30 pairs in flight, each pair = one ~60k-token prompt followed 1.5 ± 1 s later by a short (~150-token) prompt; `temperature=1.0`, `max_tokens=3000`, chat completions with `enable_thinking`. The short "follower" is admitted while the long prompt is on its 2nd–8th prefill chunk.

| variant | corrupted responses |
|---|---|
| production flags above | 15 + 2 / 400 (14 of the 200 followers); repeated on two other nodes: 12 / 400 and 9 / 400 |
| same, `--no-async-scheduling` | 14 / 400 |
| same, prefix caching off (`none` mode) | 4 / 400 (all first-step cases, as empty special-token loops) |
| same, `--max-num-batched-tokens 65536` | 6 / 400 (fewer chunked prefills, not none) |
| **no MTP** | **0 / 400** |
| **runner `reorder_batch_threshold` forced to `1 + k`** (monkeypatch) | **0 / 400**, zero misordered prefill steps in 418 |
| **drafter pinned: `"attention_backend":"TRITON_ATTN"` in `--speculative-config`** (its builder reports no threshold) | **0 / 400** |

A mixed workload (1 in 7 prompts 24k tokens, the rest 2.3k or short, 110 in flight, 1000 requests) reproduces at 0.2–1.6% with production flags and 0/1000 without MTP.

"Corrupted" = out-of-vocabulary word rate > 0.3 against the batch's own vocabulary, or > 200 completion tokens rendering to almost no text. Corrupted texts start with a coherent 5–15-word opener ("We are given a multiple choice question: \"") and then degenerate.

## Probe evidence

A `sitecustomize` probe (https://gist.github.com/filipmihal/ca652065fdd066063998c1bf6d3e9b8e, with the load generator and the analysis script) wrapped `GPUModelRunner._update_states`, `InputBatch.swap_states` and `Mamba2AttentionMetadataBuilder.build` without changing behaviour:

```
{"event": "start", "async": true, "mamba_cache_mode": "align",
 "runner_reorder_batch_threshold": 1,
 "builder_thresholds": {"Mamba2AttentionMetadataBuilder": 4, "TritonAttentionMetadataBuilder": null, "FlashInferMetadataBuilder": 1}}
```

Mamba2 prefill region of one step (`[req, num_computed_before, tokens_this_step]`): the 24k prompt's continuing chunk followed by 14 decode rows of other requests, all counted as prefills (`num_prefills = 15`):

```
[["…700f8d", 16960, 6627], ["…f9466a", 1470, 4], ["…99e300", 283, 4], ["…c17e3f", 651, 4], … ]
```

In 85 of 89 such steps the reorder recorded no swap at all (the rows were all "long_extend" at threshold 1). Across six production-flag runs with the probe, 75 of the 154 requests whose *first* decode step sat in that region were corrupted, versus 1 of 3,246 others. With the threshold forced to `1 + k`: 0 misordered steps, 0 corrupted.

With the drafter pinned to TRITON_ATTN the start line reads `"runner_reorder_batch_threshold": 4` and the FlashInfer builder is gone.

## Proposed fix

Don't let a backend that only *tolerates* a low threshold lower the threshold of a backend that *requires* ordering. PR incoming: add `requires_decode_ordering` to `AttentionMetadataBuilder` (True for the Mamba, GDN, linear-attention and short-conv builders) and have `calculate_reorder_batch_threshold` raise the minimum to the largest such builder's threshold. Attention backends already treat rows above their own threshold as prefills, so a higher global threshold costs them nothing in correctness. A more thorough fix would make the Mamba2 split independent of batch position.

Workaround for users: set `"attention_backend": "TRITON_ATTN"` (or any backend whose builder reports no threshold or `1 + k`) in `--speculative-config`, or disable MTP.

## Possibly related

- #46088 (Gemma-4 hybrid, MTP, "garbage from token 0" for short requests batched with a 64k prompt, closed "not planned") and #53180 (Qwen3.8 hybrid, MTP, intermittent degenerate output) describe the same symptom without a root cause; the mechanism above may apply if their drafter's builder reports `1`.
- #45100 (accepted-count race), #47861 / #51113 (align-mode prefix-cache snapshots) are different bugs.
